the kitchen

Everyone here just calls her Ibu Lapek

Suprapti Tanjung runs the kitchen the way she learned it in Sumatra — rendang simmered low and slow, sambal made properly hot, nothing softened for a Dutch table. Regulars from across the country, and plenty of Indonesians living far from home, come back for the same reason: it tastes like the real thing.

"Pedis is pedis" — spicy means spicy here, and no dish apologizes for it.

The menu runs deep: rendang, gulai, sambal lado ijo, soto, bakso and cendol, all made fresh, all Minang through and through. Ask your server how spicy is spicy — they'll steer you right, whether it's your first nasi padang or your hundredth.
